articles.title: Rs 5 canteen, 50% PDA quota in govt contracts: Akhilesh unveils SP's UP manifesto
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday released his party's \"PDA manifesto\" ahead of the UP assembly polls.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday released his party's "PDA manifesto" ahead of the UP assembly polls. The announcement comes on Constitution Day.The PDA, a political formulation promoted by Akhilesh Yadav, refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities). The SP has indicated that releasing its manifesto months before the polls will allow it to take its proposals to the public ahead of the election campaign.Here's what Akhliesh Yadav announcedPDA youth will be provided access to higher education through a special state education policy. The issue of paper leaks will be addressed, all examinations will be conducted on schedule, and results will be declared with complete transparency.Graduate students will be provided employment opportunities. Those who remain unemployed will receive a monthly allowance of Rs 5,000.The party will provide government jobs to 25 lakh youths and create employment opportunities across other sectors.Will begin caste-survey across the state to frame policies for the targeted upliftment.Samajwadi canteens will be set up, where meals will be available for Rs 5 per plate.Elderly women will receive Rs 40,000 as pension, with the amount transferred directly to their bank accounts.He said labourers, women workers, artisans to also receive Rs 40,000 annual pension.Laptops to be distributed again to students passing Class-12 exam, 26,000 primary schools shut by current UP government to be reopened.For government contracts worth up to Rs 50 crore, 50% reservation will be provided to members of the PDA community.The party is expected to announce two more detailed manifesto, including district, city and women-centric.In the party's election manifesto release, Akhilesh Yadav also attacked the rival BJP, saying: "When a few dominant, supremacists and selfish people want to keep their thousands of years of power intact and in that attempt want to not only amend and change but also erase the Constitution - all of us those who love the Constitution should take it up as our national and social duty to unite and thwart all conspiracies to amend the Constitution".He further said: "Our country will be governed by 'Samvidhan' (Constitution) and not 'Manvidhan' (arbitrariness). There are a few powers who want to do this through 'Manvidhan' and not 'Samvidhan'. There is an ongoing war over Constitution. On one hand, there are those who want to misue the Constitution to come to power. One the other hand is PDA, who wants the rule of social justice of the Constitution, we want to erase all differences, uphold reservation and equality..."Akhilesh Yadav's annoucement comes as relations between Congress and his party appeared to sour after the SP jumped the gun on Tuesday and announced its first list of candidates for the upcoming polls.The list was released even as deliberations over a seat-sharing deal were still ongoing between the two parties. To make matters worse, the list included candidates on two constituencies that featured on Congress' wishlist.Later, SP offered 26 seats to the Congress, which triggered unease on the second day of the seat-sharing talks for the 2027 UP polls between the two alliance partners in Delhi on Tuesday.According to reports, SP’s offer of 26 seats came after the Congress tabled a list of 120 seats of its choice.Unease was noticeable in the Congress camp over SP’s 26-seat offer as Saharanpur MP and member of Congress’s negotiating team Imran Masood objected to media claims of SP’s 36-seat offer.The SP is expected to contest the 2027 assembly elections in alliance with the Congress against the BJP-led govt in UP. The BJP has been in power in the state since 2017, while the SP governed under Akhilesh from 2012 to 2017. The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), led by Mayawati, was in power from 2007 to 2012.The 403-member UP assembly is expected to witness a major contest between the BJP and the SP-led opposition, with alliances and the mobilisation of different social groups likely to play an important role in the campaign. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the BJP won 255 seats, while its ally Apna Dal (Sonelal) secured 12.The SP won 111 seats, while its allies also won seats. The Congress secured two seats, and the BSP one. The SP received approximately 32% of the vote in the 2022 polls, emerging as the principal opposition party in the state.By choosing to release its manifesto on the Constitution Day, the SP has linked the launch of its electoral programme to a day associated with constitutional values and democratic institutions.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A retired Nevada professor lost a $475,000 battery case to his former assistant after a workplace altercation; years later, he fought to block the court-ordered sale of his Nevada home to recover the judgment
articles.summary: A retired professor who lost a $475,000 civil battery case brought by his former administrative assistant later found himself fighting to prevent the
articles.body: A retired professor who lost a $475,000 civil battery case brought by his former administrative assistant later found himself fighting to prevent the court-ordered sale of his former home in Nevada. The dispute began after a workplace altercation involving the two at Touro University Nevada. The assistant sued him and secured the judgment in 2018. Years later, after a Nevada court ordered his former residence to be sold to recover the money, the professor turned to an Ohio court to challenge the proceedings. He alleged that the original judgment involved fraudulent testimony and raised claims of elder abuse. However, the Ohio First District Court of Appeals rejected his challenge on November 25, ruling that an Ohio court could not interfere with the Nevada proceedings.Workplace altercation led to $475,000 judgmentThe case involved Yehia Marreez, a retired professor who had worked at Touro University Nevada and the University of Cincinnati, and Jackie Boiman, his former administrative assistant. Marreez lived in Henderson, Nevada, while Boiman worked at the university.Following a workplace altercation, Boiman filed a civil lawsuit against Marreez in Nevada. She secured a $475,000 judgment against him for battery in 2018.The dispute resurfaced years later when efforts were made to recover the judgment through the sale of Marreez's former Nevada residence. Court records indicated that he had transferred the property to his adult children through a quitclaim deed.Professor challenged the court-ordered saleIn December 2024, a Nevada court ordered the property to be sold to satisfy the outstanding judgment. Marreez subsequently made attempts to prevent the sale through legal proceedings in Nevada, but those efforts were unsuccessful.He also filed for bankruptcy in the Southern District of Ohio. The bankruptcy case was dismissed in February 2025, and a later request to reopen it was denied in January 2026.On December 9, 2025, Marreez filed a separate lawsuit against Boiman in Hamilton County, Ohio. He alleged that the Nevada judgment and the subsequent property proceedings were based on fraudulent testimony. He also raised claims of elder abuse and sought to stop the sale or have the judgment set aside.Boiman asked the Ohio court to dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that Marreez had failed to establish a legal basis for the relief he was seeking. The Hamilton County Court of Common Pleas agreed and dismissed the case with prejudice. Marreez then appealed the decision.Ohio appeals court rejects his challengeOn November 25, 2026, the Ohio First District Court of Appeals upheld the dismissal, ruling that the Ohio court could not intervene in proceedings involving property located in Nevada.The appeals court also rejected Marreez's elder abuse argument, finding that he had not identified an Ohio law that entitled him to the relief he sought or provided sufficient factual grounds for the claim.The judges further held that Ohio courts were required to recognise the Nevada judgment under the US Constitution's Full Faith and Credit Clause. They noted that an out-of-state judgment could not be challenged in Ohio simply because one party disagreed with its outcome. The record did not establish that the Nevada court lacked jurisdiction when it issued the judgment.The appeals panel also concluded that any request to pause the Nevada property proceedings during bankruptcy-related litigation had to be taken up with the appropriate Nevada court.It therefore affirmed the dismissal of Marreez's lawsuit, leaving the Nevada judgment and the proceedings to recover the amount outside the reach of the Ohio court.You use AI every day. The carcass was found in the Manki-Katariya forest on Wednesday, prompting a joint investigation by forest teams.3. Preliminary findings suggest the trap had been laid to catch wild boars.4. The death takes Madhya Pradesh's reported tiger mortality toll this year to at least 60.5. Forest officials are trying to identify those responsible for laying the trap and establish the circumstances leading to the tigress's death.BHOPAL: A tigress died after getting caught in a deadly clutch-wire trap allegedly laid by poachers in the Manki-Katariya forest under Panna's North Forest Division, taking Madhya Pradesh's reported tiger mortality toll to at least 60 this year.The carcass was found on Wednesday. Teams from Panna Tiger Reserve and the North Forest Division rushed to the spot and launched an investigation.Preliminary findings suggest that the clutch-wire trap had been laid to catch wild boars. The tigress got entangled in it and died. Forest officials are trying to identify those who laid the trap and establish the circumstances leading to her death.The state's reported tiger death toll stood at 59 on November 19, following the death of a male tiger in Bandhavgarh's Manpur buffer zone. The death of the tigress in Panna takes the toll to at least 60.A clutch-wire trap is designed to tighten its grip as the trapped animal struggles to escape. Each movement pulls the wire tighter around its body or limb, increasing pressure and restricting blood flow.The tightening wire can cause deep wounds, severe tissue damage and blood loss, eventually killing the animal if it remains trapped, officials said.Wildlife activist Ajay Dubey has demanded strong action in the matter, calling it a case of grave negligence on the part of forest officials. articles.title: WWE star Titus O'Neil grew up knowing what it meant to need food assistance; his foundation has now teamed with a Tampa charity to give 500 families Thanksgiving boxes, each containing meals for four to six people
articles.summary: For former WWE star Titus O’Neil, Thanksgiving is about more than a festive meal, a gathering of loved ones or a holiday tradition.
articles.body: For former WWE star Titus O’Neil, Thanksgiving is about more than a festive meal, a gathering of loved ones or a holiday tradition. It is a reminder of the difficult childhood days when putting food on the table was not always guaranteed and the kindness of others made all the difference. Now, years after overcoming those hardships, the Tampa philanthropist is helping ensure hundreds of local families experience a more hopeful holiday season.500 families receive Thanksgiving food boxesO’Neil, whose real name is Thaddeus Bullard, joined forces with Metropolitan Ministries through his Bullard Family Foundation to distribute 500 Thanksgiving food boxes to families in Tampa. The annual initiative took place Saturday morning outside the Thaddeus M. Bullard Academy at Sligh Middle Magnet School, a fitting location named in honor of the former professional wrestler.According to Spectrum News, more than 50 volunteers spent over three hours helping distribute the boxes, each containing enough food to feed four to six people. FOX 13 in Tampa Bay reported that the packages, known as Boxes of Hope, included proteins, side dishes and other essentials needed to prepare a traditional Thanksgiving meal. The distribution has become an annual tradition for O’Neil, who has maintained a partnership with Metropolitan Ministries for 11 years, the report stated.Childhood struggles inspire community workThe initiative carries personal significance for the former WWE Tag Team Champion, who experienced food insecurity growing up. After receiving support and kindness from his community when he was struggling, he is committed to helping families.O'Neil said he uses the annual distribution to fight hunger and pay forward the help that got his family through hard Thanksgivings, according to Spectrum News and Creative Loafing Tampa Bay.The need for assistance has become increasingly pressing amid rising household expenses. As reported by FOX 13 in Tampa Bay, O’Neil pointed to escalating grocery and fuel prices as factors contributing to the growing financial pressure on families.Metropolitan Ministries prepares for holiday rushThe Thanksgiving distribution is part of a much larger effort to support vulnerable households across the Tampa Bay region.Metropolitan Ministries President and CEO Sarah Combes said the nonprofit is preparing to assist 30,000 families during the Thanksgiving and Christmas season. The initiative will operate through four holiday tent locations across Hillsborough, Pinellas and Pasco counties.According to Spectrum News, O’Neil also contributed $40,000 earlier in November toward Metropolitan Ministries' Holiday Tent initiative, further strengthening the organization's seasonal assistance programme.The nonprofit's efforts extend beyond its partnership with the Bullard Family Foundation, with 35 partner organizations and community donations helping support its holiday outreach, AOL and Men's Journal reported.A legacy beyond the wrestling ringO’Neil's charitable contributions have earned recognition beyond Tampa. WWE included him in its 2020 Hall of Fame class, presenting him with the Warrior Award in recognition of his humanitarian work in Tampa and internationally. His legacy includes his wrestling achievements and his latest Thanksgiving drive to help needy families.Images Courtesy: Dave Decker/Creative Loafing Tampa BayYou use AI every day. articles.title: Two Connecticut homeowners went to court in 2019 over a utility pole that prevented them from widening their driveway; seven years later, an appeals court upheld an order requiring neighbours to authorise removal
articles.summary: A utility pole that stood in the way of two homeowners widening their driveway has remained at the centre of a dispute between neighbours in Easton,
articles.body: A utility pole that stood in the way of two homeowners widening their driveway has remained at the centre of a dispute between neighbours in Easton, Connecticut, since 2019. The disagreement began when the homeowners sought permission to remove the pole but their neighbours refused, despite an existing agreement allowing access through the property.The dispute has now reached another turning point, with the Connecticut Appellate Court upholding an order requiring the neighbours to approve the work needed to remove the pole. The decision means the homeowners can move ahead with plans to widen their driveway, subject to the utility companies carrying out the necessary work.According to legal information website Justia, the case involved Robert J. Krasko and Francis L. O'Neill, who own one property, and Robert Konkos and Chelsea Konkos, who previously owned the neighbouring property. The appeal was decided on November 10, after the neighbours challenged a 2025 ruling in favour of the homeowners.The disagreement centred on a 25-foot-wide access route connecting the homeowners' property to a public road. Although the route was meant to provide vehicle access, an old utility pole occupied part of the space needed for their driveway.Why the pole became a problemThe two properties were originally part of a subdivision created in 1978. The homeowners' plot did not have direct access to the public road, so a route across the neighbouring property was provided.In December 2015, an agreement formally gave the owner of the land without direct road access the right to use this route. It allowed people to travel across it on foot or by vehicle and permitted the construction of a shared driveway.The agreement also required the neighbouring property owners not to block access through the designated area.However, a utility pole already stood close to the middle of this route. It supplied electricity and telephone services to the neighbouring house. A second pole was installed later to serve the house built on the other property, but the older one remained because it continued to carry the neighbours' electrical connection.When Krasko and O'Neill bought the property, their driveway ran close to the older pole. They wanted to widen it but said the pole made it difficult to use the available space.They approached their neighbours for permission to have it removed. The neighbours declined, leading the homeowners to file a lawsuit in, 2019.Disagreement over cost and removal methodRemoving the old pole was not simply a matter of taking it down. The electricity connection serving the neighbours' house also had to be transferred to the newer pole.The initial proposal involved installing new electrical cables. This would have required digging up parts of the neighbours' driveway and yard, raising concerns about expense and disruption.The homeowners later suggested a different arrangement. Under the revised plan, the existing cable would be disconnected from the old pole and extended through a seven-foot trench to the newer one. A splice box would connect the cable to the new pole.This approach meant that the neighbours would not need a completely new electrical connection. The work was expected to cause only a short interruption to their electricity supply.The homeowners asked the court to require their neighbours to approve this revised plan and allow the old pole to be removed.Safety concerns and driveway width consideredDuring the trial in November 2024, both sides presented expert assessments of the driveway and the work required to widen it.The homeowners argued that the existing driveway was too narrow for comfortable and safe access. Their engineer, James Luczak, measured its usable width at eight-and-a-half feet.He also pointed to a steep drop on the opposite side of the driveway. According to his assessment, widening the driveway in that direction would require a retaining wall about 175 feet long and seven feet high.The neighbours disputed this assessment. Their experts said the driveway was wider than the measurement provided by the homeowners' engineer. They also believed that a much smaller retaining wall could provide an alternative way to expand it.The neighbours further questioned whether removing the pole was necessary, pointing out that vehicles had managed to use the existing driveway.Krasko told the court that some delivery vehicles had struggled to pass the pole. He also raised concerns about driving through the narrow space during snowy or icy conditions.The court considered these competing accounts along with photographs, property records and expert evidence.It also examined local zoning requirements. Under Easton's regulations, driveways longer than 200 feet must be at least 12 feet wide. Both sides agreed that the driveway exceeded 200 feet and was narrower than the required width.Lower court rules in homeowners' favourOn May 21, 2025, the trial court ruled that the homeowners could proceed with their proposed plan. It found that removing the pole would help address the driveway's width and safety problems. It also considered the alternative of widening the driveway on the opposite side impractical because of the drop in the ground and the engineering work involved.The court was not convinced that the revised electrical plan would cause significant problems for the neighbours. Evidence presented during the trial indicated that transferring the existing connection was routine work and could be completed by a licensed electrician.The expected interruption to the neighbours' electricity supply was estimated at two to three hours. The court therefore directed the neighbours to provide the necessary authorisation for the utility companies to remove the old pole and transfer their electrical connection to the newer one.The neighbours challenged this decision, arguing that the homeowners had other ways to widen their driveway and that the proposed work could affect their property.Appeals court upholds the orderThe Connecticut Appellate Court has now upheld the lower court's decision. It found that the homeowners had a valid right to use the access route and that their plan to widen the driveway was reasonable in the circumstances.The judges also noted that the availability of another option did not automatically mean the homeowners had to choose it. The alternative would involve substantial construction work because of the steep ground beside the driveway.The court also considered the changes since the original agreement was signed. At that time, the older pole was the only source of electricity for the neighbours' house. A second pole was installed later, making it possible to transfer the existing connection without the extensive work initially proposed.The neighbours had also argued that the lower court had granted a type of legal relief that the homeowners had not formally requested. The appellate court disagreed, saying the order specifically required the neighbours to approve the utility work. It was therefore an order to take action, not merely a statement about the parties' property rights.The appeals court affirmed the judgment in favour of Krasko and O'Neill. All three judges on the panel agreed with the decision.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Prayed for death every night': Azam Khan gets emotional about his time in jail
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan got emotional while recalling his five-and-a-half years in jail at the launch of the party's manifesto for the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan got emotional while recalling his five-and-a-half years in jail at the launch of the party's manifesto for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections on Thursday. He spoke about the fear of being killed during a jail transfer with his son, Abdullah Azam, and said he had wished party chief Akhilesh Yadav could spend six months behind bars to understand what imprisonment was like.Recalling the incident, Khan said he and his son were made to travel in separate vehicles during a jail transfer, leaving them fearing it could be their last meeting."They made me stand on one side and my son on the other, taking us in separate vehicles. When I asked why he was being taken separately, there was no answer. I told my son, 'Son, today might be our last meeting. If we don't meet here, we will meet in the hereafter,'" Khan said, adding that he prayed for death every night.He also recalled how his son would ask whether they would ever get out of jail. Khan said he wished Akhilesh could spend six months in prison to understand the hardships faced by inmates.Describing himself as a "half-broken man", Khan said the treatment he and his family had faced could have destroyed someone less resilient. He also referred to the hardships endured by his wife and son during their imprisonment."The strictness, hatred and disgust I faced should have killed me, but I proved to be tough. Now we feel, we'll die but die after achieving something," he said.Khan accused the government, jail authorities and enforcement agencies, including the Enforcement Directorate (ED), of subjecting him and his family to severe harassment. Comparing his treatment with that during British rule, he said his five-and-a-half years in a "dark cell" had taken a toll on his body, heart and mind. He also questioned the cases registered against him, alleging that charges relating to chicken theft were framed under provisions meant for dacoity, and said his legal fight to prove his innocence was continuing.The senior SP leader also recalled his five-decade association with the party and its founder Mulayam Singh Yadav, reaffirming his support for Akhilesh ahead of the 2027 polls.With Akhilesh present on the stage, Khan said, "He will be chief minister again and again, and perhaps even much more. He won't be just here; he will go much further."Khan described the newly released PDA manifesto as a blueprint for the country's future, saying the party would be willing to deliver beyond its written promises if required. The SP's PDA formulation refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities).Khan also took a swipe at AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi, without naming him directly, accusing him of trying to prevent governments from being formed rather than seeking to play the role of a kingmaker.Owaisi had recently spoken about Muslims moving beyond organising rallies to occupying positions of political power, including that of deputy chief minister. Responding to the remark, Khan had sarcastically said, "Declare my name too, make me the Prime Minister. Only the word 'Wazir' needs to be added to my name; I am already 'Azam' (Wazir-e-Azam)."Taking another veiled dig at Owaisi during Thursday's address, Khan said those troubling the SP had been given an inflated stature by their own supporters and needed to be brought back to their "original stature"."He cannot be the kingmaker, but he can spoil others' play. This is a petty and shameful goal," Khan said.Azam Khan was arrested by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) in November 2025 in a money laundering case linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, founded by him, and was lodged in Dasna district jail in Ghaziabad. The case relates to alleged financial irregularities and the acquisition of land for the university. The Allahabad High Court granted him interim bail on November 25, 2026, observing that mandatory legal provisions governing his arrest had prima facie not been followed. He was released from Dasna jail on November 26 and is headed to Rampur.His wife, former Rajya Sabha MP Tanzeen Fatima, and their son Abdullah Azam Khan were also jailed along with him in October 2023 after the three were convicted in a case involving two birth certificates issued to Abdullah. The court sentenced all three to seven years in prison. Fatima was released on bail on May 29, 2024, after spending over seven months in jail. Abdullah, a former MLA, was also granted bail by the Allahabad High Court in January 2024.Azam Khan's remarks came at the event where Akhilesh unveiled the Samajwadi Party's PDA manifesto, titled Sattais ka Sankalp: PDA ka Prannpatra, on Constitution Day. The party's PDA formulation refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities).The SP has brought forward its manifesto launch early compared with the previous two assembly elections, when it released its poll document shortly before voting. The party has said the early announcement will give it more time to take its proposals to different sections of the electorate.Read more: Rs 5 canteen, 50% PDA quota in govt contracts - Akhilesh unveils SP's UP manifestoGet the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: US district court blocks Trump’s second bid to restrict birthright citizenship
articles.summary: A US district court (Washington DC) has blocked President Donald Trump’s second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship, ruling that the administration
articles.body: A US district court (Washington DC) has blocked President Donald Trump’s second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship, ruling that the administration cannot create new exceptions to the constitutional guarantee for children born in the US.In an order dated Nov 25, Judge Christopher R Cooper certified a class of children who could be denied citizenship under the administration’s second executive order and issued a class wide preliminary injunction preventing the government from enforcing the order against them.This ruling in the case of ‘Nathan v Trump’ is the latest setback to Trump’s efforts to narrow birthright citizenship. The court held that children born in the US and subject to its jurisdiction are citizens from birth, and that the President cannot carve out additional exceptions for them.“Enough is enough,” said Cody Wofsy, deputy director of the American Civil Liberties Union’s (ACLU’s) Immigrants’ Rights Project, which was among the organisations involved in the litigation. “The Supreme Court has twice rejected efforts to gut birthright citizenship, in 1898 and again earlier this year. Third time is not the charm, and the President needs to accept that birthright citizenship is the law of the land.”The latest case concerns Trump’s second executive order on the issue, issued on Aug 6, 2026. It followed the Supreme Court’s June 30 decision in the case of ‘Trump v Barbara’, which struck down his first executive order, issued on Jan 20, 2025.The first Executive Order, sought to deny automatic citizenship to children born in the US if neither parent was an American citizen or lawful permanent resident and the mother was either unlawfully present or lawfully present on a temporary basis, such as on a tourist, student or work visa. It directed federal agencies not to recognise the citizenship of such children or issue documents recognising it.The Supreme Court rejected that approach, reaffirming the broad reach of the Fourteenth Amendment’s Citizenship Clause. The Supreme Court held that children born in the US are generally citizens because they are born subject to American law, including children whose parents are unlawfully or temporarily present in the country.The second Executive Order followed. Rather than repeat the categories covered by the first order, it sought to exclude additional groups of US-born children whose parents were not American citizens.These included children whose parents were employees of foreign governments or international organisations but did not enjoy full diplomatic immunity; children born through commercial surrogacy arrangements; and children whose parents were suspected of affiliation with certain foreign terrorist organisations or specially designated global terrorist groups. The order also addressed children born outside the statutory definition of US territory.The latest order of the Washington district court ruling blocks enforcement of the second order against the class certified by the court.The judge found that the Trump administration could not extend the narrow historical exceptions to birthright citizenship to cover these additional categories. In particular, the historical exception relating to enemy forces concerns children born during a hostile occupation of US territory, not children whose parents are merely alleged to be affiliated with a designated organisation. Similarly, the diplomatic exception applies to foreign officials enjoying full diplomatic immunity, not every person working for a foreign government or an international organisation.The district court also rejected the argument that birth tourism, commercial surrogacy or alleged parental fraud could deprive a child born in the US of citizenship. It concluded that the plaintiffs were likely to succeed on the merits and that the balance of equities and public interest favoured an injunction.Reacting to the ruling, Winnie Kao, senior counsel at the Asian Law Caucus, said: “The president keeps trying to rewrite the Constitution by executive fiat. Today’s ruling reinforces, yet again, that he cannot.”She added: “Instead of addressing the real problems Americans face, the Trump administration is wasting taxpayer dollars on yet another attempt to strip birthright citizenship from US-born babies, threatening to throw government agencies and families into chaos. Birthright citizenship has allowed generations of immigrants to build, contribute, and make this country what it is. We will continue to defend it.”The Fourteenth Amendment, ratified in 1868 after the Supreme Court’s Dred Scott decision, provides that all persons born or naturalised in the US and subject to its jurisdiction are citizens. articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed says Trump is 'tearing us apart' as he urges Americans to put politics aside this Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed urges Americans to put aside political disagreements during Thanksgiving, blaming President Trump for creating divisions. He encourages conversations focused on shared interests to reconnect with loved ones.
articles.body: Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed has urged Americans to avoid political disagreements during Thanksgiving gatherings and focus on shared interests, while accusing President Donald Trump of creating divisions among families.In a video message posted on X, El-Sayed said Thanksgiving offered an opportunity for people to reconnect with relatives and friends with whom they may have had little contact in recent years. He acknowledged that political discussions at the dinner table could become uncomfortable, particularly for families divided over recent elections.El-Sayed suggested that people consider reaching out to relatives they had not spoken to since the 2016, 2020 or 2024 elections. Rather than beginning conversations with political differences, he encouraged them to discuss everyday subjects, including family, pets and shared interests.He attributed much of the political divide to Trump, arguing that the president had become a recurring source of disagreement between Americans."Donald Trump is one neat trick," El-Sayed said in the video. "It's the ability to tear us apart, to become the subject of every conversation, and to force us to take sides."The senator-elect said finding areas of agreement could help people navigate disagreements and improve political discourse. He also acknowledged that some conversations might not be worth pursuing, but encouraged families to focus on common ground where possible.During the message, El-Sayed brought up his support for Medicare for All, a government-funded healthcare proposal he has been promoting. He argued that people could support the policy for different reasons, including empathy or a sense of duty, and said recognising those shared values could make discussions about policy differences more constructive.His comments come as Trump has indicated an interest in discussing healthcare reform with the Michigan Democrat. In an interview with the New York Post on Tuesday, the president said he planned to meet El-Sayed to discuss Medicare for All, which the senator-elect has offered to rebrand as "Trumpcare".Trump also suggested that there could be room for agreement on single-payer healthcare legislation."Maybe there's some place in the middle that we could go," the president told the publication.El-Sayed separately told Politico's Playbook that he was looking forward to speaking with Trump about healthcare, adding that even the president recognised the need for action on the issue.You use AI every day. articles.title: Udhayanidhi Stalin says Tamil Nadu CM Vijay is siding with sexual harassment accused MLA Arul Vignesh, seeks CBI probe
articles.summary: CHENNAI: Leader of the opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on Thursday accused Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay of siding with the accused rather than
articles.body: CHENNAI: Leader of the opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on Thursday accused Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay of siding with the accused rather than the victim in a sexual harassment case involving a woman district collector.Speaking after submitting a formal representation to Governor R V Arlekar, Udhayanidhi alleged that instead of arresting Kallakurichi MLA C Arul Vignesh for allegedly sending inappropriate messages to the officer, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) govt had moved the court seeking directions to remove his public statements on the incident."Why is the TVK govt yet to arrest the MLA?" Udhayanidhi asked, noting that he had urged the governor to advise the state govt to arrest Vignesh, preserve digital evidence and transfer the investigation to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI).Broadening his criticism of the administration's law and order record, Udhayanidhi claimed that nearly 700 murders had occurred since the TVK assumed office. He further alleged that ruling-party functionaries and sitting MLAs were involved in over 80% of recent criminal cases, particularly sexual offenses, citing specific incidents in his petition to the governor.Touching upon the Thiruparankundram deepam issue, the leader of the opposition pointed to the state govt's submission to the Supreme Court -- assuring compliance with judicial orders while maintaining traditional practices -- as evidence of a "double stand." He contrasted this with the previous DMK administration under M K Stalin, stating that the previous govt had stood firm, declared it would face any consequences, and ensured the lamp was lit at the customary site.In his representation, Udhayanidhi requested the governor to invoke Article 167(b) of the Constitution to obtain a comprehensive report from the chief minister regarding wider governance concerns.Among the issues flagged were an alleged assault on a petitioner by the deputy speaker in Thuraiyur, custodial deaths, cases of missing children, and major narcotics seizures -- including 137 kg of methamphetamine in Nagapattinam and 71.24 kg of heroin in Chennai -- which he alleged involved ruling-party members.Udhayanidhi called for coordinated investigations by central agencies, including the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB), Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) and the National Investigation Agency (NIA).You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chennai | Silver Rate in Chennai | Bank Holidays in Chennai | Public Holidays in Chennai | Chennai AQI | Weather in Chennai | Petrol Price in Chennai | Diesel Price in Chennai | CNG Price in Chennai | LPG Price in ChennaiStay updated with the latest Chennai news. articles.title: Congress stages show of unity in Panchkula, targets BJP over ‘vote chori’
articles.summary: Haryana Congress holds Samvidhan Raksha March in Panchkula, accuses BJP of ‘vote chori’, seeks CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s removal and voter roll restoration.
articles.body: Manvir.Saini@timesofindia.comChandigarh/PANCHKULA, November 26: The Haryana Congress on Thursday projected a show of organisational unity and political strength in Panchkula with a ‘Samvidhan Raksha March’, accusing the BJP government of undermining democratic institutions and citizens’ voting rights through alleged manipulation of electoral rolls.The march, organised on Constitution Day under the party’s nationwide campaign, was led by AICC in-charge Sanjay Dutt, Haryana Congress president Rao Narender Singh and Leader of Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda. A large contingent of Congress leaders, MPs, MLAs, former legislators and party workers participated, signalling a collective effort by the state leadership to bring the organisation together around the ‘Vote Chori’ campaign.Starting from Maharana Pratap Bhawan, the march culminated at Dr BR Ambedkar Chowk. Congress leaders and workers also collectively read the Constitution’s Preamble and pledged to protect its principles.Addressing the gathering, Sanjay Dutt accused the BJP of weakening democratic conventions, constitutional institutions and the electoral process to retain power. He said the people’s vote was not the property of any political party and asserted that Congress would oppose attempts to undermine voting rights, both on the streets and in Parliament.Rao Narender Singh said every Congress worker in Haryana was united in the struggle to protect the Constitution and democracy. He maintained that the campaign would not remain confined to a single programme but would be taken to villages and polling booths across the state.Hooda said any attack on the Constitution amounted to an attack on the democratic framework and citizens’ rights. He stressed that ensuring free and fair elections was the constitutional responsibility of the Election Commission and that concerns over the impartiality of institutions needed to be addressed.CWC permanent invitee and MP Deepender Hooda sharpened the party’s attack, demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and restoration of voters’ names allegedly deleted illegally from electoral rolls. He said the Congress would continue its agitation until these demands were met, while reiterating that questions surrounding the Haryana Assembly election process required answers.The participation of former state Congress presidents Chaudhary Virender Singh, Dharampal Malik, Ashok Tanwar and Uday Bhan, besides MPs Jai Prakash and Karmvir Boudh and several sitting and former MLAs, was also highlighted by the party as a demonstration of unity across its leadership.The march came amid the Congress’s intensified campaign over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls, giving the Constitution Day observance a distinctly political edge as the party sought to turn the issue of voting rights into a broader state-level mobilisation campaign.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: Hetero begins generic Lenacapavir shipments to Africa for HIV prevention
articles.summary: Hetero begins shipping generic injectable lenacapavir to Africa for HIV prevention, supplying 300,000 vials to Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe under Gilead’s licence.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Pharma player Hetero has begun phased shipments of generic injectable lenacapavir to Africa for HIV prevention, with an initial plan to supply three lakh vials to Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe, making the Hyderabad-based company among the first manufacturers globally to introduce a generic version of the long-acting medicine.The drug is being supplied under Gilead Sciences’ non-exclusive voluntary licence, which allows generic players to manufacture and supply to 120 eligible low- and middle-income countries. The licence covers lenacapavir for HIV prevention and for treatment of heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV. Gilead has granted the licence to six companies -- Hetero, Dr Reddy’s Laboratories, Emcure, Eva Pharma, Ferozsons Laboratories and Viatris subsidiary Mylan.Hetero said it expects to introduce generic oral initiation tablets by January 2027, completing the pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) regimen along with the injectable formulation. Until then, Gilead will continue supplying the oral component where required by national rules.Hetero managing director Vamsi Krishna Bandi said the company’s vertically integrated manufacturing network can produce 15 million vials annually and can expand further if demand rises. Hetero plans supplies to 10 additional African countries in early 2027, followed by India later.Lenacapavir, administered twice yearly, is recommended by World Health Organization (WHO) as an additional PrEP option and has shown high effectiveness in trials in reducing HIV infection risk.The rollout follows Hetero’s 2025 partnership with the Gates Foundation, backed by upfront funding and volume guarantees, and Global Fund support through its expert review panel pathway.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Hyderabad | Silver Rate in Hyderabad | Bank Holidays in Hyderabad | Public Holidays in Hyderabad | Hyderabad AQI | Weather in Hyderabad | Petrol Price in Hyderabad | Diesel Price in Hyderabad | CNG Price in Hyderabad | LPG Price in HyderabadStay updated with the latest Hyderabad news.
